svg.text: Priority operations I: grease, glaze, dust, score
Four small operations nobody had addressed, each with one passive tool and the existing turntable, spindle or manipulator.
G-assembly-meat · section 6 (6.1, 6.3, 6.9, 6.13)
grease 22 meals · glaze 7 · score 7
no consumables, no sprays in the cell
mostly conf. H
GA-30 Grease a tin: swirl-coat
reaches fluted tins (Gugelhupf) where a brush fails · 22 meals
GA-31 Glaze, egg wash: driven soft roller
surface speed = travel speed: no drag on proofed dough
GA-33 Dust: perforated dredger
laser-perforated floor, holes Ø 0.8–1.0 (0.5 for icing sugar)
GA-35 Score bread: water jet
novel, worth the test: no blade, no drag, nothing to wash
5 g oil or clarified butter dosed in
turntable tilted 60–80°, 10–20 rpm:
the liquid runs over floor, corner, wall
film 30–50 µm = 3–5 g on 1100 cm²
excess drained by inversion
flouring: 15 g flour, same motion
butter freezes on a cold tin: warm it to
40 °C or use oil · conf. H
muffin trays: 0.5 g per cavity, dabber (M)

g.text: proofed braid
shallow tray: wets the sleeve
silicone sleeve Ø 40 × 80 on the spindle
contact ≤ 0.3 N: the dough does not collapse
film 20–40 g/m² (5–8 g on a braid)
viscous glazes and icing: nozzle raster
no egg spray (raw-egg aerosol) · conf. H–M
dusted 20–60 g/m² ±30 %
shaken 5–8 Hz × 10 mm, 100–150 mm high,
moved in a raster over the work
loaded and weighed in the dry corner:
mass before − after = dose
perforated sheet, not woven mesh:
no wire crossings as crevices
rule: a powder tool is bone dry —
warm holster, never straight from the washer
family with 1 / 2.5 / 5 mm holes: garnish
proofed loaf
jet Ø 0.3–0.5 mm, mains water 4–5 bar:
stagnation pressure 400 kPa vs dough
yield stress ≈ 1 kPa
traverse 0.3 m/s, ~1 mL per 150 mm cut
the wet cut helps it open · conf. M
blade alternative: 0.4 mm, 30°, 5–8 mm deep,
drawn fast at 0.3–0.5 m/s
pork rind: steam 15–20 min, then a blade
in a depth shoe, 10 mm diamonds
1/4 Grease: 5 g of oil in the tin, tilted and turned on the turntable — the oil coats floor, corners and walls; the excess is tipped out.
2/4 Glaze: a silicone roller, wetted in a tray, is driven at exactly the travel speed so it never drags on the soft dough.
3/4 Dust: a perforated dredger, weighed before and after, is shaken in a raster above the work.
4/4 Score: a needle-thin water jet cuts the proofed loaf — no blade to drag, nothing to clean.
